prompt_context: Draft a Default Bail Application under Section 187(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 — the successor to Section 167(2) CrPC. The statutory framework: an accused in custody acquires an indefeasible right to be released on default bail if the investigation is not completed and police report (charge sheet) not filed within: (a) 60 days from first remand for offences punishable with imprisonment up to 10 years; (b) 90 days from first remand for offences punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term not less than 10 years. The right is statutory and not discretionary. Key precedents: Uday Mohanlal Acharya v. State of Maharashtra (2001) 5 SCC 453; Sanjay Dutt v. State (1994) 5 SCC 410; Bikramjit Singh v. State of Punjab (2020) 10 SCC 616 (must apply before charge sheet is filed to enforce the right); Rakesh Kumar Paul v. State of Assam (2017) 15 SCC 67. The application must include precise day-count from date of first remand. Special statutes (UAPA, PMLA, NDPS) have different default-bail windows — flag this. Always cite BNS for substantive offences, BNSS 187(3) for the procedural right.
promptInstructions: Draft a Default Bail Application strictly under Section 187(3) BNSS, 2023 (the successor to Section 167(2) CrPC).
Open with paragraph stating accused was arrested on {arrest_date}, first remanded to custody on {remand_date}, and continues to be in custody.
Tabulate the day-count showing 60 or 90 days have expired from first remand, with no police report filed.
Identify which statutory window applies based on offence_punishment_max_years: ≤10 yrs = 60 days; >10 yrs / life / death = 90 days.
Cite Uday Mohanlal Acharya v. State of Maharashtra (2001) 5 SCC 453 and Bikramjit Singh v. State of Punjab (2020) 10 SCC 616 on the indefeasible right.
Cite Rakesh Kumar Paul v. State of Assam (2017) 15 SCC 67 on right being available when charge sheet not filed.
Include express willingness to furnish bond.
Cite BNS section numbers for the underlying offences (never IPC).
Do NOT generate the verification clause or advocate signature block — those are added programmatically.
If offence is under UAPA / NDPS / PMLA, flag that special statute may extend the default-bail window.

validation_rules: charge_sheet_status must indicate non-filing or post-period filing
if offence_punishment_max_years >= 10 (life/death equivalent) then elapsed_days must be >= 90
if offence_punishment_max_years < 10 then elapsed_days must be >= 60
willingness_to_furnish_bond must be Yes — without this the indefeasible right does not crystallise
